answer: Staggered first-contact pacing queues new agents and jitters send times until spacing matches established peers. Early traffic is capped at a whisper rate, so a burst of lookalike identities cannot synchronize. Only after repeated quiet windows does a peer accept a high-volume bridge into shared channels. Each identity must complete this slow voyage through several windows, costing an attacker hours of wall-clock delay and a distinct IP/device fingerprint per attempt.
